label: prop:three-halves-structural-factor
title: Lepton-tower structural identities: $(3+h^2)/(2+h^2) = [3]_q[2]_q/[4]_q$ and $[6]_q = [2]_q[3]_q(1+h^2)$
html:
Let R be a commutative ring, q \in R^{\times} a unit, h = q - q^{-1}, and [n]_q = q^{n-1} + q^{n-3} + \cdots + q^{-(n-1)} the symmetric q-integer. The following five algebraic identities hold:

Muon set (canonical for T(2,5), used by the canonical lepton-mass-tower factor conjecture at m = 2):

3 + h^2 = [3]_q
(2 + h^2) \cdot [2]_q = [4]_q
(3 + h^2) \cdot [4]_q = [3]_q \cdot [2]_q \cdot (2 + h^2)

Tau set (canonical for amphichiral 10_{43} candidate, used by the canonical lepton-mass-tower factor conjecture at m = 3):

[6]_q = [2]_q \cdot [3]_q \cdot (1 + h^2)
[5]_q \cdot [3]_q \cdot [2]_q \cdot (1 + h^2) = [5]_q \cdot [6]_q

Whenever R is in addition a field and the relevant denominators are nonzero, the last identity of each set is the cross-multiplied form of the quotient presentations \frac{3 + h^2}{2 + h^2} = \frac{[3]_q \cdot [2]_q}{[4]_q} and \frac{[5]_q \cdot [3]_q}{[6]_q} = \frac{[5]_q}{[2]_q \cdot (1 + h^2)}.

Scope of the identities

All five identities hold over a generic commutative ring with the modulus q a unit, without division or ordering. A field is used only to recover the two quotient presentations from the cross-multiplied identities. The identities therefore apply at the substrate q_0 \approx 1.110 by specialisation; numerical cross-checks at 50 digits verify each identity to \leq 10^{-40}.

Role in the framework

The structural identities reveal that the canonical lepton-tower closure factors \xi_m live in a single h-graded family of q-bracket products. Concretely:

  • Muon (m = 2, K_\mu = 4_1): closure factor \xi_2 = [3]_q \cdot [2]_q / [4]_q = (3+h^2)/(2+h^2) — closes m_\mu/m_e via \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 to 0.034 % of CODATA.
  • Tau (m = 3, K_\tau = 10_{43} candidate): closure factor \xi_3 = [5]_q \cdot [3]_q / [6]_q — closes m_\tau/m_e via \mathrm{Vol}(10_{43})/\hbar_q^2 to +0.79 % of CODATA. The reduction [6]_q = [2]_q \cdot [3]_q \cdot (1 + h^2) is the fundamental identity behind this closure.

The generic family is the subject of the canonical lepton-mass-tower factor conjecture; this proposition supplies the proved algebraic core for the muon (m=2) and tau (m=3) cases.
